text.text: Known failure modes
Ways each tool is known to fail, each with the run that showed it and a source you can open. 9 entries, shown on 10 tools and inputs; 8 open, 1 fixed.
Data from 15 Oct 2026, commit 4a4b1171 (source)
Filter the entries

Each entry is one item of a file failure_modes/<tool>.yaml (schema). On every push, scripts/failure_modes.py --check fetches each source from GitHub and fails if a quote is not in it character for character, or if a number in the finding is not in a quote. An entry shows on its tool's card; an entry about an input (the Pfam truth set, the AlphaFold models) shows only here.

kmerseek kmerseek 0.4.0 keys each index entry by its k-mer set, so two different sequences with the same k-mer set become one entry and the second is lost. In a regions-index pilot, 6 of 99_232 rows reported residues that are not at the target's own coordinates; the PR traces this to the key but has not confirmed it for each of the 6. In an index of 125 ribonucleases built on a later branch with the same key, 31 are missing under cys2 and 7 under cys_hp3.open · the number: 6 of 99_232 rows; 31 of the 125 ribonucleases · reported 10 Oct 2026 in seanome/kmerseek PR 141, seanome/kmerseek PR 148What to do: Rebuild every 0.4.0 index once kmerseek PR 141 is merged; it keys each entry by its sequence. Until then, a recall number from a 0.4.0 index is measured against a reference that may be missing targets.In the 2024-kmerseek-analysis regions-index pilot (kmerseek v0.4.0, protein20, k=5), 6 of 99_232 rows had a target_subseq that is not target[target_start:target_end].seanome/kmerseek PR 141Two different sequences with the same k-mer set get the same sum. So the second entry's hits came out with the first entry's coordinates and residues.seanome/kmerseek PR 141Not done: rebuilding the pilot index and rechecking the 6 rows. entries.finding: In the ELM motif run, Foldseek was scored on orthologs that have no AlphaFold model. It cannot search those, so its share of motifs found is low for a reason that is not the search.

entries.number: median 5 to 21 residues early; 45% to 60% more than 100 residues early

entries.run: `make leaderboard-pileup` and the region pile-up page (Figure 4)
entries.what_to_do: Read a call's ends as the alignment's ends, not the domain's. To score where a domain sits, place the target's domain through the alignment.

entries.finding: kmerseek 0.4.0 keys each index entry by its k-mer set, so two different sequences with the same k-mer set become one entry and the second is lost. In a regions-index pilot, 6 of 99_232 rows reported residues that are not at the target's own coordinates; the PR traces this to the key but has not confirmed it for each of the 6. In an index of 125 ribonucleases built on a later branch with the same key, 31 are missing under cys2 and 7 under cys_hp3.

evidence.quote: In the 2024-kmerseek-analysis regions-index pilot (kmerseek v0.4.0, protein20, k=5), 6 of 99_232 rows had a `target_subseq` that is not `target[target_start:target_end]`.
Two different sequences with the same k-mer set get the same sum. So the second entry's hits came out with the first entry's coordinates and residues.

Not done: rebuilding the pilot index and rechecking the 6 rows. The two rows that are not anywhere in the target fit this cause, but I have not confirmed which earlier entry each of the 6 targets was merged into.
An index keys each entry by its k-mer set, so two sequences with equal sets collapse into one entry and only the first is stored.
That is why 31 of the 125 ribonucleases are absent under `cys2` and 7 under `cys_hp3`.

entries.run: the regions-index pilot (kmerseek v0.4.0, protein20, k=5), and the 125 test ribonucleases searched with topi ribonuclease (P00659)
entries.what_to_do: Rebuild every 0.4.0 index once kmerseek PR 141 is merged; it keys each entry by its sequence. Until then, a recall number from a 0.4.0 index is measured against a reference that may be missing targets.

entries.finding: The exact Poisson score (`region_poisson_score`) stops at 307.65, where the p-value underflows. In 102 of 107 exact settings, decoy pairs reach that ceiling, so the decoy-matched cutoff sits above it and those settings find nothing.

evidence.quote: `region_poisson_score` stops at 307.65, which is -log10 of the smallest normal double: the Poisson p-value underflows. In 102 of 107 exact settings, at least two tune decoy-family pairs reach that ceiling. The matched cutoff then sits just above it, and those settings find nothing at all.
b215e87 scores the exact arm on `region_tfidf` (Olga, 2026-10-14; recorded in nb 280's first cell).

entries.run: the time-split pilot's tune half, 186 settings (notebook 280)
entries.what_to_do: Compute the p-value in log space inside kmerseek. Until then, score exact settings on `region_tfidf`, as notebook 280 now does.

entries.finding: Three rounds of profile search gave dipeptide-shuffled decoy proteins hits as strong as E 1e-22. One round gave them none below E 0.026. So with three rounds, a cutoff matched to decoys is set by the profile's own drift toward a family.

evidence.quote: The 3-round profile search gave dipeptide-shuffled decoys hits down to E 1e-22, and one round gives none below E 0.026.

entries.what_to_do: Run one round (`--num-iterations 1`) when a cutoff is matched to decoys, or set the cutoff separately for each number of rounds.

entries.finding: 9 Pfam truth domains lie partly or wholly past the end of their protein's QfO sequence, for example P15692 PF14554 342–395 on a 232 aa protein. The Pfam coordinates come from a different version of these sequences.

evidence.quote: Found: 9 Pfam truth domains lie partly or wholly past the end of their protein's QfO sequence, for example P15692 PF14554 342–395 on a 232 aa protein. The Pfam coordinates come from a different version of these sequences.
